title: Variable TTL prefetch strategy and field-trial orchestration for cache-sensitive workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Static TTLs for KV/prefix cache and one-size-fits-all prefetch cause unnecessary memory retention and missed savings on low-value requests. We need a variable time-to-live (TTL) prefetch policy plus an orchestration layer to run controlled field trials that reliably measure cost, latency, and quality impact across workload cohorts and rollout stages.

This initiative will: design a variable TTL prefetch policy that adapts TTL per key or key-class via lightweight heuristics and model-informed predictors; build the orchestration primitives to schedule, monitor, and analyze multi-cohort field trials; and provide safe rollout primitives (canary, throttle, automatic rollback) tied to quality and cost SLOs. It aims to reduce token-inference unit cost by reducing unnecessary cache retention while preserving tail latency and model output quality.
goals: Reduce average cache memory footprint for low-hit keys by >=25% in test clusters
Demonstrate net per-token cost reduction >=6% in controlled field trials without degrading p95 latency by >5%
Ship trial orchestration UI + API to create cohorts and gates for easy experimentation by Platform and Product teams
scope: Design variable TTL policies (heuristics + ML-lite predictor) for KV/prefix cache
Implement runtime TTL controller and eviction telemetry hooks into serving runtime
Build field-trial orchestration: cohort assignment, metric collection, automated canary gates, and rollback actions
Experiment harness and dashboards for cost/latency/quality analysis
Safety: explicit quality gates (prompt set evals) and traffic throttles
success_metrics: Cache memory utilization delta (baseline vs trial) as measured in staging clusters
Per-token cost delta in trial cohorts (billing simulator + real usage)
Quality regression flag rate on curated prompt sets < 2% relative to baseline
milestones: M1: Policy design and simulation framework complete (2025-01-31)
M2: Runtime TTL controller + telemetry merged to staging (2025-02-14)
M3: Field-trial orchestration API + minimal console flows available (2025-02-28)
M4: First external pilot with two customer cohorts (2025-03-14)
M5: Post-pilot analysis + rollout decision and runbook (2025-03-28)
risks: Quality regressions not detected by small eval sets -> need to expand prompt coverage
Eviction oscillation for keys near threshold causing jittered latency spikes
Telemetry resolution may be insufficient to attribute cost changes to TTL policy alone
rollout_plan: Stage: internal staging cluster with synthetic and production-like traffic for 2 weeks
Canary: 1% production traffic cohort with aggressive rollback gate on quality or p95 latency
Ramp: linear increase to 25% over 4 days if gates hold
Pilot: run 2 customer pilots (non-critical workloads) for 3 weeks
Global: default policy release behind tenant-level opt-in toggle; promote to default after no regressions for 6 weeks
acceptance_criteria: Policy telemetry shows expected TTL distribution and eviction rate in staging
Dashboards show cost/latency/quality comparison for all cohorts
Automated canary gates trigger rollback on predefined thresholds during internal canary
Documentation and runbook published to Confluence and linked in the ticket
Security review completed (no sensitive data exposure in telemetry)
